title: Etale closed-support bounds for the transported pro-etale exceptional functor
statement:
Fix the finite purity coefficients [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell
e\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$; put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with quasi-compact complementary open immersion $j:W\hookrightarrow T$. Suppose $(W,T)$ satisfies the ordinary etale open-complement condition at $A$ with an integer $c\geq0$ [def-exc-open-complement-bound]. Write $i_e^!$ for the ordinary etale right adjoint to closed direct image, and let $Ri^!=
u_Z^*i_e^!R
u_{T,*}$ be the transported functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], with $
u_S:S_{\mathrm{proet}}	o S_{\mathrm{et}}$ the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For integers $r\leq s$ the following two assertions hold separately.

1. If $B\in D_c^{[r,s]}(T,A)$ [def-weil-constructible-intervals], there is a bounded constructible ordinary etale complex $B_e$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:
u_T^*B_e\cong B$, with $\mathcal H^t(B_e)=0$ for $t
otin[r,s]$. For any such witness there is a natural identification
$$Ri^!B\cong
u_Z^*i_e^!B_e,$$
and
$$Ri^!B\in D_c^{[r,s+c+1]}(Z,A).$$
No finite-Tor hypothesis is imposed on $B$ in this assertion.
2. If $B\in D^b_c(T,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] has pro-etale Tor amplitude in $[r,s]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], then every bounded constructible etale witness $B_e$ for $B$ has etale Tor amplitude in $[r,s]$, meaning $\mathcal H^t(B_e\otimes_A^LM_e)=0$ for every degree-zero etale $A$-module sheaf $M_e$ and $t
otin[r,s]$. The object $Ri^!B$ is bounded constructible and has pro-etale Tor amplitude in $[r,s+c+1]$, tested against every degree-zero pro-etale $A$-module sheaf on $Z$, whether or not it comes from the etale site.
